pictures.scene: Homer, The Fog Warning — one lone fisherman out on an open sea in a small wooden dory that is riding up the back of a swell, leaning on his oars in a heavy dark coat and a black oilskin hat with his bearded face turned in profile to look back over the water, two great pale halibut lying in the bottom of the boat behind him, a keg and coiled line beside them, white water breaking all along the dark waves below and a long grey bank of cloud coming up across a worked pale sky, simon peter told them, i am going fishing, …
pictures.name: pd_homer_mistwaarschuwing

pictures.scene: Witz, The Miraculous Draught of Fishes — one enormous Christ standing at the water's edge in a great scarlet mantle that falls in heavy folds right down to the ground, seen from the side with His face in profile and a worked red-and-gold halo behind His head, reaching out one hand toward the lake, an old bearded man in a dark coat wading out toward Him up to his waist with an arm lifted, a long wooden boat behind them with men bending over the side to haul up a net out of the green water and another standing up in it in a brilliant red robe, and beyond them a wide worked valley of green fields, hedges, a white farm, a little red-roofed tower and dark hills under a pale sky, early in the morning, jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was jesus, …
pictures.name: pd_witz_fischzug

pictures.scene: Sorolla, Fisherman with His Nets — one weathered fisherman filling the whole height of the picture as he walks forward over stony brown ground with a great dark fishing net hauled up over his shoulder and trailing away behind him in a long heavy swag, a yellow cloth bound round his head, a worn open shirt and a dark sleeveless jacket hung with cork floats, a red sash knotted at his waist, canvas trousers rolled at the ankle and both feet bare, one hand gripping the net above his head and the other arm thrown wide open, with low white houses, a beached hull and a bare mast behind him under a blue sky full of worked white cloud, cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some, …
pictures.name: pd_sorolla_netten

pictures.scene: van Beyeren, Still Life with Fish — a heaped wicker basket of freshly caught fish standing on a plank table in a dim kitchen, their wet silver sides catching the whole of the light so that they shine out of the brown dark, a big round-eyed fish lying open-mouthed across the top of the pile, two long fish laid over the basket rim, a broad cut of salmon glowing deep orange-pink behind them, a flat fish hanging over the near edge, a crumpled grey-green cloth below with a bone-handled knife and a small skimmer beside it, a copper cooking pot standing in the shadow at the left and a wooden board hung on an iron hook above, when they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread, …
pictures.name: pd_beijeren_stilleven_met_vissen

pictures.scene: Sorgh, Market by the Harbour — a quayside market stall set up under a wooden penthouse with the brown sails of moored boats standing up behind it against a worked sky, a flat round basket of small silver fish and a cut fish laid open on the board, baskets of greens beside it and a great heaped basket of carrots and cabbages spilling across the whole bottom of the picture, a seated market woman in a scarlet jacket with a white collar and a wide black hat holding out a dish to a young housewife in a rose-red bodice and a long white apron who has come up with her pail, a smiling man in a dark cloak and a broad hat leaning over the stall between them, a small child in a white cap looking out from behind and another man in a red cap at the back, jesus told them, bring some of the fish you have just caught, …
pictures.name: pd_sorgh_markt_am_hafen

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, The Supper at Emmaus — a dim worked stone hall with a great dark arch rising over the whole upper half, and under it a small round table spread with a brilliant white cloth that takes all the light, Christ seated at the middle of it in a pale rose robe with a grey mantle over His knee and a faint glow of light standing out all round His head, breaking a loaf in both hands and looking straight out with His lips parted, a young disciple at the left leaning back on his chair with his hands lifted and his bare feet beneath him, an old bearded disciple at the right thrust forward in a brown coat with his hand laid flat on the cloth, and a serving boy bending in behind him carrying a dish of food, pewter plates, a glass and a knife on the table, jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and he did the same with the fish, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Mauve, The Return of the Flock — a great flock of sheep coming straight toward us up a worked brown heath, their heavy fleeces packed so close that the whole middle of the picture is a drift of cream and grey wool, one small white lamb standing alone in a gap among them and looking out, the shepherd a dark figure in a cap and long coat walking away at the top of the flock with his crook over his shoulder and his back turned, a low brown rise running right across behind him with a few dark tufts of heather, worked rough grass and sandy track spreading out to the bottom edge, and a quiet pale sky above with two or three birds in it, jesus replied, feed my lambs, …
pictures.name: pd_mauve_flock

pictures.scene: Plockhorst, The Good Shepherd — one full-height Christ walking straight toward us down a stony track with His head bent and His eyes lowered, in a deep crimson robe belted at the waist under a long pale grey mantle, a soft gold halo round His hair, a small lamb gathered up in the crook of His arm against His breast with its legs hanging down and His hand holding it, a tall shepherd's staff in His other hand, His bare feet on the rough brown path, three sheep pressing up close at His left and two more at His right, and behind them a green bank with thin trees, a pale stretch of water and a quiet sky, jesus told him, shepherd my sheep, …
pictures.name: pd_plockhorst_the_good_shepherd

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Tears of Saint Peter — one huge aged apostle filling the picture with his head tipped back and his wet eyes lifted up, his white hair and thick white beard catching the light and his mouth a little open, wrapped in a great golden yellow mantle thrown across his shoulder over a deep blue-green robe, his two bare forearms brought together low in front of him and his hands clasped tight, a pair of heavy iron keys hanging from a cord at his wrist, a dark worked brown rock behind him with trailing green ivy coming down on both sides and a pale glimpse of sky at the left edge, but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_saint_peter_in_tears

pictures.scene: Friedrich, Two Men Contemplating the Moon — two travellers standing together on a stony path at dusk, both seen squarely from behind in long dark green coats, the nearer one in a flat cap leaning in with his hand laid on his companion's shoulder and his face turned to him in lost profile, the other in a fur cap holding a staff, a thin crescent moon with a warm glow about it hanging low in a graded evening sky before them, a great gnarled oak and a dark fir spreading their bare crooked branches right across the whole top of the picture, and a bank of torn earth and roots with scattered boulders falling away below, peter turned and saw the disciple whom jesus loved following them, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_two_men_contemplating_the_moon

pictures.scene: de Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — a tall whitewashed gothic church worked all over with pale arches, round pillars and clear leaded windows, a preacher in black leaning out of a high wooden pulpit with his hand put out as he speaks, rows of small dark hats and faces banked up behind the panelled screen below him, a great brass chandelier hanging in the middle, and in the near shadow a little group that is not listening at all, a woman in a black hood with a wide white collar and red sleeves bending to speak with a man, a small boy in a yellow coat and a white apron standing beside her, another woman kneeling in a heavy black cloak, a brown and white dog sitting up in a bar of daylight on the swept flagstones, and a hooded woman with her back turned at the right edge, because of this, the rumor spread among the brothers, …
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

pictures.scene: Spitzweg, The Bookworm — one old scholar standing high up on a library ladder in a great room whose walls are shelved with books from the floor to the carved cornice, holding an open volume close to his face and reading it in a shaft of light, another book gripped in his other hand, a third clamped under his arm and a fourth held fast between his knees, in a black coat and knee breeches with a white neckcloth and a handkerchief hanging from his pocket, a gilded scroll over the case beside him lettered with the name of its subject, two carved busts set along the top, a painted ceiling above, and a dark globe standing in the shadow at the bottom corner, not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written, …
pictures.name: pd_spitzweg_boekenwurm

lines.text: Later, by the Sea of Tiberias, Jesus again revealed Himself to the disciples. He made Himself known in this way: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two other disciples were together.
Simon Peter told them, I am going fishing. We will go with you, they said. So they went out and got into the boat, but caught nothing that night.
Early in the morning, Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not recognize that it was Jesus.
So He called out to them, Children, do you have any fish? No, they answered.
He told them, Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some. So they cast it there, and they were unable to haul it in because of the great number of fish.
Then the disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, It is the Lord! As soon as Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment, for he had removed it, and jumped into the sea.
The other disciples came ashore in the boat. They dragged in the net full of fish, for they were not far from land, only about a hundred yards.
When they landed, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread.
Jesus told them, Bring some of the fish you have just caught.
So Simon Peter went aboard and dragged the net ashore. It was full of large fish, 153, but even with so many, the net was not torn.
Come, have breakfast, Jesus said to them. None of the disciples dared to ask Him, Who are You? They knew it was the Lord.
Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and He did the same with the fish.
This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.
When they had finished eating, Jesus asked Simon Peter, Simon son of John, do you love Me more than these? Yes, Lord, he answered, You know I love You. Jesus replied, Feed My lambs.
Jesus asked a second time, Simon son of John, do you love Me? Yes, Lord, he answered, You know I love You. Jesus told him, Shepherd My sheep.

Jesus asked a third time, Simon son of John, do you love Me? Peter was deeply hurt that Jesus had asked him a third time, Do you love Me? Lord, You know all things, he replied. You know I love You. Jesus said to him, Feed My sheep.

Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted; but when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and lead you where you do not want to go.
Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. And after He had said this, He told him, Follow Me.
Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them. He was the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper to ask, Lord, who is going to betray You?
When Peter saw him, he asked, Lord, what about him?
Jesus answered, If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you? You follow Me!

Because of this, the rumor spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. However, Jesus did not say that he would not die, but only, If I want him to remain until I return, what is that to you?
This is the disciple who testifies to these things and who has written them down. And we know that his testimony is true.
There are many more things that Jesus did. If all of them were written down, I suppose that not even the world itself would have space for the books that would be written.
